interpretation: Post-hoc descriptive service-cost reanalysis; pointwise bootstrap intervals, no confirmatory superiority decisions
arity_log2_exposure: sum histogram count * arity * log2(arity), float64 sensitivity proxy; not an exact integer core endpoint
weights: 7 held-out traces equally per parent; 20 parents equally per model; 3 models equally per size; 4:3 ID:shift combined; phases and sizes separate; registered binary bracket arms equally within source panel
ratio: E[C]/E[S] with identical parent/model weights; cost per accepted request, not E[C/S] and not cost per accepted value
normalization: accepted count, value and total cost also reported per attempted request C/H and S/H; H=12*n
interval: pointwise unadjusted 95% percentile intervals; inverse ECDF nearest rank, one-based 500 and 19500; not simultaneous intervals
pairing: shared parent-stratified resampling across all arms and costs; contrasts are source minus its registered binary panel, plus DA minus FHS5
undefined: zero service denominator is null; report trace/parent zero counts and undefined bootstrap count; any undefined draw disables that cell interval rather than conditioning by deletion
checkpoint: one raw block at a time; gzip bootstrap sums in 500-replicate chunks; exclusive lock; PAUSE boundary; hashes bind config/code/runtime/evidence
limitations: Route exposure proxies do not measure real communication bytes, latency, fees or cryptographic implementation cost.
Totals depend on achieved service; interpreting lower total cost alone as efficiency is invalid.
Intervals are exploratory and pointwise; no p-values, multiplicity-adjusted decisions, causal claims or population equivalence claims.
Arity-log2 exposure and its intervals use floating point; exact rational estimates retained for integer metrics.
This audit checks saved routes and arithmetic, not routing optimality or a new blinded simulation replay.
